- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks, especially in early 30d window.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates lows; increase forecast lows, especially in late 30d window.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp sentiment spikes (e.g., sentiment jumps to 1.00), leading to overprediction in 3–5 day horizon; apply dampening factor to post-spike values.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d forecasts: if forecast is >2.5σ above recent mean, reduce by 15–30% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- Sentiment volatility (rapid swings) correlates with forecast instability: if sentiment changes >0.5 in 3 days, reduce forecast confidence and apply smoothing filter to 30d output.
- Early 30d forecasts (days 1–7) often overpredict; apply downward bias of 10–20% if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- Late 30d forecasts (days 24–30) often underpredict; apply upward bias of 10–20% if sentiment is negative or trending down.
